sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Show that } f(x) = e^{-x^2/2} \text{ is self-reciprocal under Fourier transform.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(F(s) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-1}^{1} (1-x^2) e^{i s x} dx\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Use Euler's formula and even/odd symmetry: integral of odd part vanishes}\)

(1 Mark)

\(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot 2 \int_{0}^{1} (1-x^2) \cos(s x) dx\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Integrate by parts or use standard integral formula}\)

(2 Mark)

\(= \frac{4}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{\sin s - s \cos s}{s^3}\)

sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find the Fourier transform of } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1-x^2 & |x| \le 1 \\ 0 & |x| > 1 \end{cases}.\)

lq.ANSWER:
1. Apply the definition of Fourier transform

2. Integrate and obtain F(s) 

3. Take Inverse Fourier transform to F(s)

4. Obtain the answer \(-\frac{3\pi }{16}\)

StepMarks
\(F(s) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2/2} e^{isx} dx\)(2)
Complete the square: \(-\frac{x^2}{2} + isx = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 2isx) = -\frac{1}{2}[(x - is)^2 + s^2]\)(3)
\(F(s) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-s^2/2} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-(x-is)^2/2} dx\)(3)
The integral \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-(x-is)^2/2} dx = \sqrt{2\pi}\) (using contour integration)(3)
Thus \(F(s) = e^{-s^2/2}\)(2)
